extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists and academic professionals; specifically crystallographers, zoologists, geologists, engineers, and medical/surgical practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative commentary and correspondence in an academic journal covering how to judge scientific books, technical primers, and experimental reports; includes letters discussing experimental conventions and taxonomic evidence. Focuses on criteria for clarity, accuracy, reproducibility, and practical usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of detrital minerals for stratigraphical correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: “the evidence provided by detrital minerals is rather unsafe as a basis of stratigraphical correlation, owing to the rarity and local significance of instances in which detrital minerals are derived from what he calls ‘homogeneous distributive provinces.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overgeneralising from scarce or locally-significant mineralogical occurrences; require broad, representative data across systems/series before using detrital-mineral composition as a basis for stratigraphical correlation or palaeogeographical inference. Emphasise further patient fact-collecting before asserting substantial utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and representativeness of data for generalisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique noting that ‘‘the facts available are as yet scanty and very local in their significance’’ and therefore conclusions should be cautious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure datasets are sufficiently large, geographically and stratigraphically representative before drawing broad conclusions; explicitly state limitations of available evidence in arguments and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of methods and apparatus coverage in technical texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanical testing volume is praised because it provides information regarding modern methods of testing and apparatus not found in college laboratories or brief textbook sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical treatises should describe sampling/treatment, apparatus, test methods, and practical procedures in enough detail that practitioners and students lacking specific equipment can understand and evaluate methods. Include diagrams and operational descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of comparative/benchmark values
rubrics_metrics.description: “Sufficient information is given regarding the results of methods of testing to enable the experimenter to compare his own results with average values for trustworthy materials.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include average/benchmark values and guidance for comparing experimental outcomes to accepted standards, enabling readers to assess material quality and test accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical completeness and detail in clinical/prosthetic handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosthetics handbook includes a chapter on amputation stumps (characteristics of a good stump, conditions preventing fitting), classified prostheses by work and amputation region, illustrations, and an appendix with specifications and fitting directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical/technical handbooks should cover pre-fitting clinical conditions, classification of devices by function and anatomical site, detailed fitting and fabrication instructions, maintenance/repair guidance, and specifications in appendices to be clinically actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy in concise technical primers
rubrics_metrics.description: The industrial nitrogen primer is ‘‘very brief but readable’’, but several minor inaccuracies were noted (e.g., incorrect yields, incorrect reagents, misattributed references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even short primers must ensure factual correctness of process descriptions, yields, reagents, and citations; minor factual errors can mislead readers and undermine utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, arrangement, and scope appropriate for student textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: The organic-chemistry textbook ‘‘follows the usual lines. Only important compounds are described, and attention is directed to the general relationships between groups of compounds. The style is clear and the matter well arranged’’ and is useful to students when supplemented by lectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should balance breadth and depth (focus on important examples), emphasise relationships and systematics, use clear prose and good structure, and note intended use cases (e.g., as a companion to lectures). Production quality (printing/paper) also affects usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of diagrams and clarity of descriptive text
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for works where ‘‘the diagrams are well drawn and the descriptions are clear’’ (e.g., motor control and switchgear primers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, well-labelled diagrams that directly support the textual descriptions; good visual aids are essential in technical explanations and improve accessibility for students and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policy on anonymous communications and responsibility for opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial note: ‘‘The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters and correspondence should be signed and attributable; editors disclaim responsibility for correspondents' views—authors should ensure identification and provide contact details as per journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specimens/data for verification and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Author states ‘‘the regenerating larve are at the disposal of any one who may wish to control my figures.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make physical specimens, data, figures, or other primary materials available to other researchers for verification; explicitly note availability and access conditions in publications or correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate classificatory/taxonomic claims via authorities and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Author wrote to leading authorities to ask their opinions on asteroid primitiveness and quoted their responses to support taxonomic argumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making classificatory claims, consult and cite relevant experts and the published literature; present correspondence or authoritative opinions where appropriate to situate claims within current expert consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and state a convention for optical rotation (Biot vs Herschel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion: two conventions exist (Biot’s table-polariscope convention vs Herschel’s convention looking along the beam); ‘‘It is very important that this should be quite clear.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a convention (the author and many recommend Biot’s) and state it explicitly in text/figures; avoid switching conventions without clear explanation; clarify how clockwise/anticlockwise and right/left-handed labels are being applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify experimental conditions when reporting optical-rotation observations
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘‘It is thus important to know the exact conditions of the experiment whenever the question of the correct discrimination of right- or left-handed-ness in the optical rotation of crystals is being dealt with.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report instrument configuration (table polariscope vs projection), observer viewpoint (looking with or against the beam), orientation of plates, and whether projection inverts handedness; clarify which experimental setup the convention refers to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use single, untwinned crystals and identifiable faces for unambiguous handedness determination
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘‘The safest course, in the case of quartz, is to cut the section-plate to be used to afford the definite decision from a crystal which is clearly a single individual, and not a twin, showing the little s and x faces unmistakably.’’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and document single-crystal specimens showing characteristic faces to avoid misidentification due to twinning; prepare sections accordingly and report crystal morphology used to determine optical handedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise, unambiguous language when describing optical phenomena (definition of 'ascend'/'descend')
rubrics_metrics.description: Confusion arose in successive editions of Pereira’s book where the terms used to describe the colour order on Newton’s scale were inconsistent (e.g., ‘descend’ vs ‘ascend’ used oppositely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define directional or ordinal terms explicitly (e.g., give the sequence of colours or reference plate behaviour) and avoid contradictory phrasing across editions; ensure consistent usage throughout a work so students/readers are not confused.
